```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE,
  fig.width=9, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160)
```

L0glm combines a fast GIC preset with compiled adaptive-ridge solvers to recover
sparse models with accurate effects and few false positives. These examples
compare complete fitting and selection workflows, with known simulated truth
used to assess both speed and recovery.

## One million predictor example

<!-- BEGIN million-intro -->
This Gaussian simulation has **one million predictors**, 1,000 observations and 60 nonzero effects. One default L0glm call takes **3.61 seconds** and recovers **46 true effects with no false positives**.
<!-- END million-intro -->

L0glm uses its default GIC preset with ISIS screening and criterion-checked support refinement.
LASSO and fully relaxed LASSO search paths of up to 40 lambda values, selected
by BIC or five-fold CV. BIC is included because GIC can select an empty LASSO
model at this dimension; all methods are also evaluated using the common GIC.

<!-- BEGIN million-comparison -->
| Method | Selection | Seconds | GIC | TP | FP | FN | TN | F1 | MCC |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **L0glm + ISIS** | **GIC preset** | **3.61** | **4195** | **46** | **0** | **14** | **999940** | **0.868** | **0.876** |
| LASSO | BIC path | 41.03 | 5789 | 34 | 20 | 26 | 999920 | 0.596 | 0.597 |
| Relaxed LASSO | BIC path | 42.55 | 18650 | 43 | 753 | 17 | 999187 | 0.100 | 0.197 |
| LASSO | 5-fold CV | 205.98 | 14106 | 42 | 373 | 18 | 999567 | 0.177 | 0.266 |
| Relaxed LASSO | 5-fold CV | 188.73 | 4475 | 31 | 1 | 29 | 999939 | 0.674 | 0.707 |
<!-- END million-comparison -->

```{r million-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.2, dev.args=list(pointsize=18), fig.cap="Fitting time, true-effect recovery and false positives in the million-predictor example. L0glm uses a GIC preset; both LASSO methods use five-fold CV. There are 60 true effects."}
layout(matrix(1:3, nrow=1), widths=c(1.3, 1, 1))
par(mar=c(4, 6.5, 2.8, 1), mgp=c(2.5, .6, 0), family="sans", cex.axis=.85,
  bg="white", col.axis="#34465d", col.lab="#34465d", col.main="#0a1930")
labels <- c("L0glm + ISIS", "LASSO", "Relaxed LASSO")
cols <- c("#087e83", "#8b5cc7", "#d04a78")
seconds <- c(3.61, 205.98, 188.73)
plot(seconds, 3:1, log="x", xlim=c(min(1, min(seconds)/2), max(seconds)*1.8), ylim=c(.6, 3.4), pch=21, bg=cols,
  col=cols, cex=2.2, yaxt="n", xlab="Seconds (log scale)", ylab="", bty="n")
axis(2, at=3:1, labels=labels, las=1, tick=FALSE, cex.axis=.9)
abline(v=c(1, 10, 100), col="#e1ebef", lty=3)
points(seconds, 3:1, pch=21, bg=cols, col=cols, cex=2.2)
text(seconds, 3:1, sprintf("%.2f s", seconds), pos=ifelse(seconds > 50, 2, 4),
  offset=.8, cex=.8, col="#29455a")
title("Fast fitting and selection", adj=0, cex.main=1.1)
par(mar=c(4, 1, 2.8, 1))
tp <- c(46, 42, 31)
plot(tp, 3:1, xlim=c(0, 68), ylim=c(.6, 3.4), pch=21, bg=cols, col=cols,
  cex=2.2, yaxt="n", xlab="True positives (of 60)", ylab="", bty="n")
text(tp+2, 3:1, tp, pos=4, cex=.9, col="#29455a")
title("True effects recovered", adj=0, cex.main=1.1)
fp <- c(0, 373, 1)
plot(fp, 3:1, xlim=c(0, max(10, max(fp)*1.3)), ylim=c(.6, 3.4), pch=21, bg=cols, col=cols,
  cex=2.2, yaxt="n", xlab="False positives", ylab="", bty="n")
text(fp+.03*max(10, max(fp)), 3:1, fp, pos=4, cex=.9, col="#29455a")
title("Fewer false positives", adj=0, cex.main=1.1)
layout(1)
```

<!-- BEGIN million-speed -->
L0glm is **57× faster than five-fold-CV LASSO** in this comparison, recovering **46 true effects with no false positives**.
<!-- END million-speed -->

See the [high-dimensional tutorial](high-dimensional.html) for the data setup
and comparisons with SIS/ISIS screening applied to the other methods too.

## Abess benchmark problems

These higher-dimensional extensions of the Gaussian and logistic examples in
the [abess documentation](https://abess-team.github.io/abess/articles/v11-power-of-abess.html)
use **20,000 predictors** with AR(1) correlation 0.3 and signed effects of
absolute size 0.35–0.8. Test scores and recovery metrics are means across three
independent replications; elapsed times are medians.

L0glm uses its GIC preset and automatically applies a
[local support search](../reference/local_search.html) to small initial
solutions with **50 or fewer coefficient dimensions**. The other methods
select from paths of up to 40 lambda values using the common GIC; ABESS searches
support sizes 0–100. LASSO and fully relaxed LASSO are also tuned by five-fold CV.

**Gaussian regression: 500 observations and 40 true effects.** L0glm matches
ABESS's GIC and support recovery in **0.37 s versus 1.80 s**. Compared with
CV LASSO, it recovers all 40 effects with an average of just 0.7 false positives
and lower test RMSE.

<!-- BEGIN difficulty-gaussian -->
| Method | Selection | Test RMSE | TP | FP | F1 | MCC | Seconds |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| L0glm | GIC preset | 1.037 | 40.0 | 0.7 | 0.992 | 0.992 | 0.37 |
| ABESS | GIC path | 1.037 | 40.0 | 0.7 | 0.992 | 0.992 | 1.80 |
| L0Learn | GIC path | 1.060 | 40.0 | 0.3 | 0.996 | 0.996 | 0.78 |
| LASSO | GIC path | 3.781 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.97 |
| Relaxed LASSO | GIC path | 2.276 | 24.0 | 7.3 | 0.663 | 0.684 | 1.30 |
| Adaptive LASSO | GIC path | 3.552 | 5.3 | 0.0 | 0.190 | 0.211 | 1.75 |
| Adaptive relaxed LASSO | GIC path | 2.942 | 13.7 | 0.3 | 0.496 | 0.570 | 1.64 |
| MCP | GIC path | 1.019 | 40.0 | 0.0 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.29 |
| SCAD | GIC path | 2.020 | 26.7 | 2.7 | 0.635 | 0.636 | 1.87 |
| LASSO | 5-fold CV | 1.899 | 39.7 | 282.3 | 0.219 | 0.347 | 5.86 |
| Relaxed LASSO | 5-fold CV | 1.727 | 39.0 | 188.0 | 0.364 | 0.460 | 6.55 |
<!-- END difficulty-gaussian -->

**Logistic regression: 1,000 observations and 20 true effects.** L0glm fits in
**0.54 s** with no false calls in these replications. CV LASSO takes 10.11 s
and retains an average of 217.3 false positives. ABESS and L0Learn recover
slightly more true effects, with longer fitting times.

| ABESS | GIC path | 0.871 | 16.3 | 0.3 | 0.886 | 0.893 | 8.64 |
| L0Learn | GIC path | 0.871 | 16.3 | 0.3 | 0.886 | 0.893 | 11.85 |
| LASSO | GIC path | 0.605 | 3.7 | 0.3 | 0.229 | 0.237 | 1.79 |
| Relaxed LASSO | GIC path | 0.863 | 15.0 | 0.7 | 0.833 | 0.842 | 9.43 |
| Adaptive LASSO | GIC path | 0.850 | 15.7 | 0.7 | 0.850 | 0.863 | 2.52 |
| Adaptive relaxed LASSO | GIC path | 0.856 | 14.0 | 0.0 | 0.819 | 0.834 | 7.65 |
| MCP | GIC path | 0.842 | 13.7 | 0.0 | 0.808 | 0.824 | 3.02 |
| SCAD | GIC path | 0.675 | 3.7 | 0.3 | 0.229 | 0.237 | 5.55 |

| Relaxed LASSO | 5-fold CV | 0.846 | 14.3 | 1.0 | 0.812 | 0.821 | 49.45 |

## Single sample deconvolution

A blurred Poisson spike train has **10,000 observations, 10,000 candidate peak
positions and 1,000 true peaks**. L0glm achieves **F1 0.845 in 0.14 s** with
one GIC preset. Fully relaxed LASSO tuned by five-fold CV takes 2.77 s and
achieves F1 0.534.

<!-- BEGIN single-metrics -->
| Method | Selection | Seconds | GIC | TP | FP | FN | TN | F1 | MCC |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| L0glm | GIC preset | 0.17 | 102765 | 845 | 154 | 155 | 8846 | 0.845 | 0.828 |
| LASSO | GIC path | 0.40 | 145904 | 950 | 2096 | 50 | 6904 | 0.470 | 0.467 |
| Relaxed LASSO | GIC path | 0.64 | 122083 | 905 | 999 | 95 | 8001 | 0.623 | 0.607 |
| LASSO | 5-fold CV | 4.83 | 146234 | 951 | 2146 | 49 | 6854 | 0.464 | 0.462 |
| Relaxed LASSO | 5-fold CV | 6.70 | 133122 | 920 | 1523 | 80 | 7477 | 0.534 | 0.524 |
<!-- END single-metrics -->

All fits are evaluated with the original Poisson likelihood. LASSO uses a
weighted Gaussian approximation with weights `1/(y+0.1)`, searching ten lambda
values by GIC or five-fold CV. The [deconvolution tutorial](deconvolution.html)
shows fitted signals and coefficient comparisons.

## Multichannel deconvolution

The GC/MS-style problem has **10,000 scans, 10,000 candidate peak positions,
1,000 true peaks and all 226 informative mass channels**. Joint row selection
recovers peak times, while coefficients within each row describe the mass
spectrum.

<!-- BEGIN multi-speed -->
L0glm recovers **944 of 1,000 true peaks with 11 false positives** in **11.34 seconds**. In this benchmark it is **21.6× faster than GIC-tuned group LASSO** and **282× faster than relaxed group LASSO tuned by five-fold CV**.
<!-- END multi-speed -->

<!-- BEGIN multi-metrics -->
| Method | Selection | Seconds | GIC | TP | FP | FN | TN | F1 | MCC | Within-row F1 | Within-row MCC |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| L0glm | GIC preset | 11.34 | 5606331 | 944 | 11 | 56 | 8989 | 0.966 | 0.962 | 0.912 | 0.869 |
| Group LASSO | GIC path | 244.87 | 7413616 | 980 | 860 | 20 | 8140 | 0.690 | 0.685 | 0.842 | 0.768 |
| Relaxed group LASSO | GIC path | 906.34 | 6138687 | 909 | 309 | 91 | 8691 | 0.820 | 0.802 | 0.853 | 0.782 |
| Group LASSO | 5-fold CV | 813.42 | 9639345 | 998 | 4242 | 2 | 4758 | 0.320 | 0.316 | 0.886 | 0.830 |
| Relaxed group LASSO | 5-fold CV | 3199.62 | 6198648 | 962 | 502 | 38 | 8498 | 0.781 | 0.769 | 0.856 | 0.785 |
<!-- END multi-metrics -->

Within-row F1 and MCC assess spectral sparsity among correctly recovered peaks.
L0glm fits the Poisson model with channel-specific working weights. Group LASSO
uses a Gaussian approximation with shared row weights `1/(rowMeans(y)+0.1)`;
ten lambda values are selected by GIC or five-fold CV. Fully relaxed fits use
`gamma=0`. See the [deconvolution tutorial](deconvolution.html) for heatmaps,
coefficient plots and complete code.

## Reproduce and extend

* [Million-predictor example and plots](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmark_website_examples.R)
  and [LASSO comparison workflows](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmark_million_lasso.R).
* [Higher-dimensional Abess benchmark problems](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmark_support_difficulty.R)
  and [complete results and fitting notes](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/plots/website/support-difficulty-runs.csv).
* [Single and multichannel deconvolution workflows](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmark_website_deconvolution.R).
* [`sparseGLM()`](../reference/sparseGLM.html) applies the same comparison framework to your own data.
* [File-backed Gaussian and logistic GWAS examples](file-backed.html) include
  an 80 GB design: L0glm takes **249 s** versus **792 s** for BIC-tuned biglasso
  LASSO, with **one versus three false positives** and lower held-out RMSE.
* [Predictor-group comparisons with grpreg](predictor-groups.html) cover group
  LASSO, MCP and SCAD with equal and unequal group sizes.

Benchmarks were run on an **HP ZBook Fury 17.3-inch G8 Mobile Workstation**
with an **Intel Core i9-11950H at 2.60 GHz**, **8 physical and 16 logical cores**,
using Windows, R 4.5.0 and OpenBLAS. BLAS uses one thread. The million-predictor
example uses eight screening threads, with CV folds evaluated serially.
The Abess benchmark problems use one thread throughout. Multichannel
deconvolution uses four fitting threads and deconvolution CV uses four parallel
workers; single channel fitting uses one thread.

Timings include fitting and selection, and exclude simulation and final metric
reporting. Million-predictor LASSO workflows use fresh R sessions to bound
memory, with input loading and session startup excluded. Deconvolution CV
timings include parallel-worker startup. The million-predictor L0glm timing is
the median of three runs. CV comparisons use shared folds. Known coefficients
are used only for evaluation. The reproduction scripts specify scoring floors,
approximation choices and all simulation settings.
